top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

able to read one file and run two commands without guessing.

top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does

    concurrency:

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

statically-discoverable test command — repo is unrunnable

by far the cheapest. Drop an AGENTS.md at the repo root that names a
canonical entry point and a canonical test command, then back those
claims with the actual files (`[project.scripts]` in pyproject.toml,
`test:` target in a Makefile, etc.). The goal is for an agent to be
able to read one file and run two commands without guessing.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
No agent-targeted docs, no conventional entry point, and no
statically-discoverable test command — repo is unrunnable
end-to-end by an agent.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Pick the lightest of the three to add first — agent-targeted docs are
by far the cheapest. Drop an AGENTS.md at the repo root that names a
canonical entry point and a canonical test command, then back those
claims with the actual files (`[project.scripts]` in pyproject.toml,
`test:` target in a Makefile, etc.). The goal is for an agent to be
able to read one file and run two commands without guessing.

top_findings.message: 5 findings — e.g. Hotspot: cc-prompt.md changed 326 times and is >200 lines.; Hotspot: meta/cli-surface.md changed 278 times and is >200 lines.
top_findings.fix_hint:
For each hotspot, identify the dominant axes of change (e.g. one
file holds both API routing and validation logic) and split along
those lines. After the split, both halves see lower per-file churn.

top_findings.message: 5 findings — e.g. At least one entry-point convention is present. (no clause matched); Manifest pyproject.toml not present.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `[project.scripts]` table to pyproject.toml mapping a CLI
name to your `module.cli:main` entry point. For Go, add
`cmd/<name>/main.go`. For Node, set `"bin"` or `"main"` in
package.json. The goal: an agent running `--help` on the package
should find a command that works.

A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

    concurrency:

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

package.json. The goal: an agent running `--help` on the package
